newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica financial stocks rebound from heavy losses.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica financial stocks rebound from heavy losses.

text.p: Financial stocks rebounded strongly on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Wednesday recovering from hefty falls on Tuesday, analysts said.

"The index is up mainly on Liberty Life. In response to a sharp fall yesterday (Tuesday). The market was more harsh on the financial stocks than industrials," Doug Ellish, analyst at Standard Equities told Reuters.

Liberty Life Association of Africa Ltd gained 200 cents to 127 rand in a volume of 117,200 shares valued at nearly 15 million rand. On Tuesday it lost 175 cents to close at 125 rand. Analysts said Liberty had a big weighting in the index.
On Wednesday the financial index peaked at 7,669.7 before settling at 7,645.7, 39.4 points or 0.52 percent up on the day.
Dealers said bargain hunters fuelled the index's rise.
South African shares ended a volatile day marginally firmer with all-shares 0.35 percent up at 6,891.8, industrials 0.13 percent up at 8,124.7 and golds up 0.12 percent up at 1,708.1.
Analysts said the financial index did much to prop up the all-share index.
On Tuesday the financial index lost 160.8 points, or 2.11 percent, to 7,606.3 amid fears that the rand crisis would trigger an interest rate hike, analysts said.
A fresh bout of speculation on Wednesday sent the already sickly rand below 4.70 bid on the dollar for the first time. It was last trading at 4.7325 bid.
Amalgamated Banks of South Africa (Absa) closed 20 cents higher at 24 rand, First National Bank Holdings easing 20 cents to 25.70 rand.
Standard Bank Investment Corporation was steady at 175 rand and Nedcor Ltd added 125 cents to 65.50 rand.
Dealers said bargain hunters lifted the index.
